headline: TopKLoRA paper reports sparse causal circuits for removing known-trigger backdoors
summary: A new preprint presents TopKLoRA, a sparse fine-tuning adapter, with a Contrastive Latent Circuit Discovery pipeline for locating behaviors introduced during fine-tuning. In synthetic sleeper-backdoor model organisms up to 7B parameters, the authors report that ablating a selected circuit removes nearly all held-out responses to a known syntactic trigger, while multi-layer adapters retain benign instruction-following. The study compares against dense LoRA and reports smaller, more specific circuits. These are author-reported results in a controlled setup; unknown or semantic triggers, larger models, and independent reproduction remain open.
